classification: NUMERICAL ARTIFACT of the recurrence in its non-convergent regime

evidence.test: Solver C spectral contrast at the candidate frequency
evidence.interpretation: Solver C sees NO root: sigma_min at the candidate is LARGER than at a generic nearby frequency. At a genuine QNM Solver C shows contrast ~1e11.

evidence.test: Solver A depth convergence at these parameters (ordinary mode)
evidence.interpretation: Solver A does NOT converge here. Its CF residual stays ~1e-13 while the root itself drifts -- the residual measures the truncated equation, not the truncation error, exactly as documented in docs/PRECISION_VALIDATION.md.

evidence.test: three-solver spread on an ordinary mode at the same parameters
evidence.interpretation: The three solvers agree only to ~3.5e-3 in this region. A repeated-root diagnostic of 4.3e-6 is three orders of magnitude BELOW the frequency uncertainty, so it carries no information.
Solver C is internally stable across contour length and resolution, so the 3.5e-3 spread is not Solver C's error alone.

verdict: The small |dF/domega| was produced by Solver A's non-convergent drift in a regime where the Leaver series is only slowly convergent (r2 = 0.44 against a validated domain of r2 <~ 0.20). It is NOT evidence of a repeated root. The candidate is refuted as an EP2.
mechanism: Near extremality the spurious singularity x(-r_+) = 2 r_+/(r_+ + r_-) approaches the unit circle, so the Frobenius series radius of convergence degenerates. The continued fraction then returns depth-dependent roots whose residual is small but whose value drifts.
what_would_be_needed: A method that resolves the near-horizon scale r_+ - r_- = 0.094 directly -- multidomain spectral matching or near-horizon matched asymptotics (the near-extremal/ZDM treatment) -- to reach better than 1e-3 accuracy in this region.
not_claimed: This does not prove no EP exists near extremality; it shows this candidate is not evidence of one.
